summary: BBN's report on ARPANET host status for November 8 to 19, 1971. It lists hosts that were excluded from the daily tests and notes changes, such as hosts becoming servers or users. It was replaced by RFC 287.

eli5.summary: Another check-up report on which network computers were up, and who could be visited.

questions: when did sdc become arpanet server
subtitle: ARPANET host status for November 8-19, 1971, noting new users and servers.

tldr.problem: ARPANET operators needed to track the growing number of nodes and their changing roles as servers or users.
tldr.mechanism: BBN continued biweekly status reports with daily reachability tests and updates on which hosts were excluded from testing.
tldr.outcome: Lincoln's TX2 became a user host, and SDC's IBM-360 became a server, continuing the network's growth.

today: RFC 267 is Historic and has been obsoleted by RFC 287. It documents the ARPANET's continued growth in November 1971.

sections.title: Introduction and Exclusions
sections.content: RFC 267 reports on ARPANET host status from November 8 to November 19, 1971. On November 18 the BBN Terminal IMP was offline for hardware debugging. The report lists hosts excluded from daily testing in two categories: those not expected to be servers for at least two weeks (Rand PDP-10, Lincoln TX2, Case, Carnegie, Ames B6500 and IBM-360), and user-only hosts (Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center). During this period, Lincoln's TX2 became a network user and SDC's IBM-360 became a server.
sections.eli5: A report from mid-November showed which computers were tested, which ones were skipped, and noted that one computer changed from being tested to being left alone.

sections.title: Daily Test Results
sections.content: Two tables summarize host status for November 8-12 and November 15-19 (November 18 was excluded due to Terminal IMP downtime). Tests used status codes where O meant open, D meant dead, T meant timeout, H meant half-open, and R meant refused. Some sites advertised unavailable times. UCLA's IBM-360 is now explicitly noted to provide Remote Job Service only, without a Telnet server.
sections.eli5: Tables showed each day's test results for 12 hosts, using the same letter codes to mark how each computer responded.

sections.title: Host Predictions and Server Status
sections.content: The report includes host status predictions from operators, showing expected dates when hosts would become servers (for example, Case predicted March 1972, Carnegie predicted January 1972). Most major hosts like UCLA, SRI NIC, UCSB, and MIT Multics were servers or soon would be. SDC was now confirmed as a server after this period. Some hosts like Stanford and Illinois remained user-only or had uncertain status.
sections.eli5: Site operators said when their computers would be ready to help others, and the test results showed which ones were already working.

references.text: Wentheimer, E., "Network host status", RFC 255, October 1971.
